reviewer.method: Direct assessment of complete corrected English/Ukrainian message, typed parameters and every one of 50 named memberships in two 25-member batches. Current result-wire/result-verify producer inspected directly. Python used only to project, hash, bind and serialize actual bytes, not create semantic judgments. No external completion calls.

findingDispositions.currentNative: Саме отримання захищеного результату ще не надає перевірених байтів даних. Результати, захищені лише щодо цілісності, можна прочитати до перевірки, але їм ще не можна довіряти; для {protected1} не можна заявляти виявлення втручання в тіло. Операція {protected2} та результати не є невідкличними токенами авторизації на майбутнє.
findingDispositions.rationale: The corrected first sentence now says receipt alone does not provide verified data bytes, removing the mistaken entitlement-to-bytes claim. Integrity-only readability before verification, lack of body-tamper claims for {protected1}, and absence of irrevocable future authorization from {protected2}/results all remain complete. Ukrainian grammar and both protected tokens are preserved. Actual corrected bytes match the original complete proposed correction and are effective for both originally reported keys and all fifty family members.
findingDispositions.closureScope: This finding on corrected actual Native schema 1353, all 50 explicit detail/protocolDetail members, at the recorded current catalog hash only. Original report remains immutable.

observations: Wire receipt explicitly does not establish client acceptance.
Failed local result verification produces no accepted file bytes.
Successful verification locally decrypts/stores accepted result and sets clientAccepted/clientBytes.
clientBytes binding requires actual plain accepted result.

records.english: Protected receipt never grants bytes. Integrity-only results are readable untrusted before verification; {protected1} cannot claim body tamper detection. {protected2}/results are not irrevocable future authorization tokens.
